record.original_question: Classify all geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane that have exactly three unbalanced vertices.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1.5. Classify all geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane with 3 unbalanced vertices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Work in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. A geodesic multinet is a finite connected graph $\Gamma$ embedded in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose vertex set $V(\Gamma)$ is finite and whose edges are straight line segments (geodesics), with the convention that multiple edges between the same pair of vertices and isolated loops are allowed only insofar as each edge is realized as a (possibly degenerate) straight segment; each edge $e$ is assigned a positive integer multiplicity $m(e) \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$.

For a vertex $v \in V(\Gamma)$ and an edge $e$ incident to $v$, let $u_{v,e} \in \mathbb{R}^2$ denote the unit vector at $v$ pointing along $e$ away from $v$. The vertex $v$ is called balanced if
$$\sum_{e \ni v} m(e)\, u_{v,e} \;=\; 0,$$
and unbalanced otherwise. (Equivalently, a geodesic multinet is the 1-skeleton of a stationary integer 1-varifold in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose stationarity may fail at a prescribed finite set of vertices, the unbalanced ones.)

Problem. Provide a complete classification, up to similarity of $\mathbb{R}^2$, of all geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane that have exactly three unbalanced vertices. The classification should describe the combinatorial structure (graph with edge multiplicities), the possible positions of the unbalanced vertices and of any additional balanced vertices, and the resulting straight-edge embeddings.
artifact.status_search_result: For ordinary geodesic nets (all edges multiplicity one) with three unbalanced/boundary vertices in a non-positively curved plane, it is known (Parsch, J. Differential Geom. 119 (2021)) that there is at most one balanced vertex, located at the Fermat point of the three unbalanced vertices, giving the classical Fermat-Torricelli configuration. However, the broader classification problem for geodesic multinets (allowing edge multiplicities) with three unbalanced vertices does not appear to have been resolved in the literature; subsequent work (e.g., on four-boundary-vertex multinets, 2024–2025) continues to treat such classification questions as open.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: A geodesic net with three boundary vertices on a non-positively curved plane has at most one balanced vertex... located at the Fermat point.
status_evidence.claim: Settles the unit-multiplicity case (geodesic nets, not multinets) with three boundary vertices.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Continues exploration of classification of geodesic (multi)nets with few boundary vertices.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats classification of geodesic multinets with few unbalanced vertices as ongoing.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets with Few Boundary Points (thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey/thesis discussing open problems on geodesic nets and multinets.
status_evidence.claim: Lists multinet classification questions among ongoing problems.
